name: TUM G06 scaled wind turbine (D = 0.6 m, RG-14, very low Reynolds number, pitch and wind-speed sweeps)

rg14.polar_source: RG14 polars of the TUM G1 (TWEET-IE dataset section_10.dat, Re 47k-84k) reused; the tuned G06 polars of the paper are not published

experiments.conditions: UTD BLAST boundary-layer tunnel, 2.8 m x 2.1 m, blockage 4.8 % (uncorrected), TI 0.15 %, uniform inflow; U = 10 m/s; collective pitch 0/2/3/4/6 deg (column pitch_deg); rpm varied (tsr 4-8.5)
experiments.source: Nanos et al. 2022, Fig. 8a (Cp) and 8b (Ct), digitised (extraction/digitise_fig8.py)
experiments.uncertainty: digitising: tsr +-0.03, cp +-0.004, ct +-0.005 for 'marker' rows, about double for 'line' rows; measurement: loads ~1 %, pitch +-0.3 deg

experiments.conditions: same tunnel, pitch 0 deg, U = 6/7/8/9/10 m/s (column v_ms): Reynolds-number dependence of Cp/Ct
experiments.source: Nanos et al. 2022, Fig. 8d (Cp) and 8e (Ct), digitised
experiments.uncertainty: as above; several 6-9 m/s markers are hidden under the 10 m/s curve and are missing (only points that were visible are kept)

sources.citation: Nanos E.M., Bottasso C.L., Manolas D.I., Riziotis V.A. (2022). Design, steady performance and wake characterization of a scaled wind turbine with pitch, torque and yaw actuation. Wind Energy Science 7, 1263-1287.
TWEET-IE blind test Phase I dataset (TUM G1 model, RG14 polars). Zenodo, CC-BY-4.0.

notes: Very small rotor (D = 0.6 m) at chord Re ~2e4-6.5e4 (see extraction/check_tum_g06.png): the strongest low-Reynolds test of the suite, with Cp AND Ct for five pitch angles and five wind speeds. EVERYTHING IS DIGITISED: geometry from Fig. 2 (c/R and twist vs r/R), performance from Fig. 8 (see the overlays in extraction/). The blade is modelled from r/R = 0.06 (Rhub = 0.018 m); inboard of that the figure shows a cylindrical root (c/R 0.067) not modelled - its contribution is negligible. Twist is plotted as 'blade twist' and taken to be the solver convention (chord angle to the rotor plane without pitch, positive to feather) - the paper does not state the reference explicitly; the tip value ~0.5-2 deg and the stated optimum at beta = 0 support it. Polars: the paper tunes RG-14 polars from G06 measurements (Fig. 9) but does not publish them; the TUM G1 RG14 polars (Re 47k-84k, themselves identified from G1 rotor measurements) are reused, so below Re ~4.7e4 (outboard at U = 6-7 m/s, and the whole blade at low tsr) the solver extrapolates in Re - expect the 6-7 m/s curves to be the hardest to match. Density and viscosity are not given in the paper (UTD, Dallas, ~180 m a.s.l.): rho = 1.18, nu = 1.55e-5 assumed; cp/ct do not depend on rho directly. Blockage 4.8 %, no correction applied by the authors.
